1	# TIOBE Programming Community Index -- March 2026 Monthly Report
     2	
     3	## Source
     4	
     5	- URL: https://www.tiobe.com/tiobe-index/
     6	- Captured: April 10, 2026
     7	- Author: Paul Jansen, CEO, TIOBE Software
     8	
     9	The TIOBE Programming Community Index is a widely cited indicator of programming language popularity, updated monthly since 2001. Ratings are calculated from the number of skilled engineers worldwide, training courses, and third-party vendors, using search-engine hit counts across Google, Amazon, Wikipedia, Bing, and more than 20 other sites. The index does not measure which language is "best" or which has the most lines of code written; rather, it reflects how much a language is discussed and sought after on the public internet.
    10	
    11	## March 2026 Headline: Why the TIOBE Index Still Relies on Search Engines
    12	
    13	The March 2026 editorial addresses a recurring question: should the TIOBE index switch from search-engine hit counts to LLM-based assessments of language popularity? Paul Jansen explains that the answer is no. LLMs are ultimately trained on the same web pages that search engines index, so querying an LLM would not yield fundamentally different data. The methodology therefore remains anchored to direct measurement of web-page volume per language.
    14	
    15	Beyond the methodology discussion, the March update records several notable rank changes. SQL and R swapped positions within the top 10, with R climbing from 16th to 9th year-over-year. Swift re-entered the top 20 at the expense of Kotlin, and Ruby is on the verge of dropping out of the top 30.
    16	
    17	## Top 20 Programming Languages -- March 2026
    18	
    19	![Top 20 programming languages ranked by TIOBE rating, March 2026](./assets/table_top20_rankings.jpg)
    20	
    21	| Rank (Mar 2026) | Rank (Mar 2025) | Programming Language | Rating | YoY Change |
    22	|:---:|:---:|------|:---:|:---:|
    23	| 1 | 1 | Python | 21.25% | -2.59% |
    24	| 2 | 4 | C | 11.55% | +2.02% |
    25	| 3 | 2 | C++ | 8.18% | -2.90% |
    26	| 4 | 3 | Java | 7.99% | -2.37% |
    27	| 5 | 5 | C# | 6.36% | +1.49% |
    28	| 6 | 6 | JavaScript | 3.45% | -0.01% |
    29	| 7 | 9 | Visual Basic | 2.50% | -0.02% |
    30	| 8 | 8 | SQL | 2.00% | -0.57% |
    31	| 9 | 16 | R | 1.88% | +0.94% |
    32	| 10 | 10 | Delphi/Object Pascal | 1.80% | -0.36% |
    33	| 11 | 24 | Perl | 1.75% | +1.05% |
    34	| 12 | 12 | Scratch | 1.63% | -0.03% |
    35	| 13 | 11 | Fortran | 1.45% | -0.25% |
    36	| 14 | 14 | Rust | 1.31% | +0.09% |
    37	| 15 | 15 | MATLAB | 1.29% | +0.31% |
    38	| 16 | 7 | Go | 1.29% | -1.49% |
    39	| 17 | 17 | Assembly language | 1.29% | +0.42% |
    40	| 18 | 13 | PHP | 1.23% | -0.25% |
    41	| 19 | 18 | Ada | 1.10% | +0.25% |
    42	| 20 | 26 | Swift | 1.04% | +0.44% |
    43	
    44	Python holds the top position at 21.25%, more than double the rating of second-place C (11.55%). However, Python's year-over-year change is -2.59 percentage points, while C gained +2.02 points. The top 4 languages -- Python, C, C++, and Java -- collectively account for nearly 49% of the total index.
    45	
    46	## Historical Trend: Two Decades of Language Popularity (2002--2026)
    47	
    48	![Historical popularity trends for the top 10 programming languages from 2002 to 2026](./assets/chart_historical_trends.jpg)
    49	
    50	The TIOBE index publishes a long-running trend chart covering the top 10 languages from 2002 to the present. Key patterns visible in the data:
    51	
    52	- **Python's meteoric rise**: From a minor language ranked around 8th in 2006, Python surged to the top position after 2018, peaking above 25% before settling at 21.25% in March 2026.
    53	- **C's resilience**: C has held a top-2 position for most of the 24-year span, with periodic surges (notably around 2015 and again in 2025--2026).
    54	- **Java's long decline**: Java dominated the index from roughly 2005 to 2018, but has steadily fallen from the 25%+ range to under 8%.
    55	- **JavaScript's plateau**: Despite its dominance in web development, JavaScript has never exceeded roughly 5% on the TIOBE index and currently sits at 3.45%.
    56	
    57	## Very Long Term History: Rank Positions Across Four Decades
    58	
    59	![Long-term ranking history of selected programming languages from 1986 to 2026](./assets/table_long_term_history.jpg)
    60	
    61	| Language | 2026 | 2021 | 2016 | 2011 | 2006 | 2001 | 1996 | 1991 | 1986 |
    62	|------|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|
    63	| Python | 1 | 3 | 5 | 7 | 8 | 26 | 17 | - | - |
    64	| C | 2 | 1 | 2 | 2 | 2 | 1 | 1 | 1 | 1 |
    65	| C++ | 3 | 4 | 3 | 3 | 3 | 2 | 2 | 2 | 9 |
    66	| Java | 4 | 2 | 1 | 1 | 1 | 3 | 31 | - | - |
    67	| C# | 5 | 5 | 4 | 5 | 7 | 11 | - | - | - |
    68	| JavaScript | 6 | 7 | 8 | 10 | 10 | 8 | 33 | - | - |
    69	| Go | 10 | 11 | 60 | 16 | - | - | - | - | - |
    70	| Ada | 14 | 36 | 25 | 22 | 16 | 18 | 6 | 10 | 3 |
    71	| Lisp | 26 | 34 | 26 | 13 | 14 | 19 | 8 | 4 | 2 |
    72	
    73	This table reveals dramatic shifts across decades. Python was unranked before 1991, entered the top 30 only by 2001, and took 25 years to reach the top position. Conversely, Lisp was the number-2 language in 1986 but has fallen to 26th. Ada peaked at 3rd in 1986 and now sits at 14th. C is the only language that has remained in the top 2 across all nine measurement points.
    74	
    75	## Programming Language Hall of Fame
    76	
    77	![Hall of Fame -- Language of the Year winners from 2003 to 2025](./assets/table_hall_of_fame.jpg)
    78	
    79	The TIOBE "Programming Language of the Year" award goes to the language with the largest gain in ratings during a calendar year. Recent winners include:
    80	
    81	| Year | Winner |
    82	|:---:|------|
    83	| 2025 | C# |
    84	| 2024 | Python |
    85	| 2023 | C# |
    86	| 2022 | C++ |
    87	| 2021 | Python |
    88	| 2020 | Python |
    89	| 2019 | C |
    90	| 2018 | Python |
    91	| 2016 | Go |
    92	
    93	Python has won the award five times (2007, 2010, 2018, 2020, 2021, 2024), more than any other language. C# took the title in both 2023 and 2025, reflecting its continued growth driven by the .NET ecosystem.
    94	
    95	## Key Findings
    96	
    97	- **Python remains dominant but is losing ground**: At 21.25%, Python leads by a wide margin, yet its year-over-year decline of -2.59 percentage points is the largest drop among the top 5. C, by contrast, gained +2.02 points and climbed from 4th to 2nd.
    98	- **Legacy languages show surprising resilience**: Perl jumped from 24th to 11th (+1.05%), R rose from 16th to 9th (+0.94%), and Fortran remains in the top 15. These languages continue to serve entrenched communities in scientific computing, data analysis, and infrastructure.
    99	- **Go suffers its sharpest decline**: Go fell from 7th to 16th, losing 1.49 percentage points -- the largest absolute drop of any top-20 language. This contrasts with its 2016 "Language of the Year" win and suggests possible displacement by Rust (14th, +0.09%) in the systems programming space.
   100	- **Swift re-enters the top 20, Kotlin exits**: Swift climbed from 26th to 20th (+0.44%), while Kotlin dropped to 22nd. In the mobile development ecosystem, Swift's gains may reflect Apple platform growth, while Kotlin faces competition from cross-platform frameworks.
   101	- **The top 4 languages hold nearly half the index**: Python, C, C++, and Java together account for 48.97% of total TIOBE ratings, illustrating how concentrated the programming landscape remains despite 50+ tracked languages.

Slide 1: Title slide with methodology intro
Slide 2: Top 20 Rankings with table/bar chart

from pptx import Presentation
from pptx.util import Inches, Pt
from pptx.dml.color import RgbColor
from pptx.enum.text import PP_ALIGN, MSO_ANCHOR
from pptx.enum.shapes import MSO_SHAPE
from pptx.oxml.ns import nsmap
from pptx.oxml import parse_xml
import os

# Create presentation 16:9
prs = Presentation()
prs.slide_width = Inches(13.333)
prs.slide_height = Inches(7.5)

# Color palette - professional data-forward
DARK_BG = RgbColor(0x1A, 0x1F, 0x2E)       # Dark navy background
ACCENT_TEAL = RgbColor(0x2D, 0xC4, 0xBA)   # Teal accent
ACCENT_CORAL = RgbColor(0xE8, 0x5D, 0x4C)  # Coral accent
ACCENT_GOLD = RgbColor(0xF4, 0xB9, 0x3E)   # Gold accent
TEXT_WHITE = RgbColor(0xF5, 0xF5, 0xF5)
TEXT_GRAY = RgbColor(0xB0, 0xB8, 0xC8)
TABLE_HEADER = RgbColor(0x25, 0x2D, 0x3D)
TABLE_ROW1 = RgbColor(0x1E, 0x24, 0x33)
TABLE_ROW2 = RgbColor(0x22, 0x2A, 0x3A)
POSITIVE = RgbColor(0x4C, 0xD9, 0x7A)
NEGATIVE = RgbColor(0xE8, 0x5D, 0x4C)

def add_background(slide, color=DARK_BG):
    background = slide.background
    fill = background.fill
    fill.solid()
    fill.fore_color.rgb = color

def add_textbox(slide, left, top, width, height, text, font_size=18, bold=False, color=TEXT_WHITE, align=PP_ALIGN.LEFT, font_name="Calibri"):
    txBox = slide.shapes.add_textbox(left, top, width, height)
    tf = txBox.text_frame
    tf.word_wrap = True
    p = tf.paragraphs[0]
    p.text = text
    p.font.size = Pt(font_size)
    p.font.bold = bold
    p.font.color.rgb = color
    p.font.name = font_name
    p.alignment = align
    return txBox

def add_shape_text(slide, left, top, width, height, text, font_size=14, bold=False, color=TEXT_WHITE, fill_color=None, align=PP_ALIGN.CENTER):
    shape = slide.shapes.add_shape(MSO_SHAPE.RECTANGLE, left, top, width, height)
    if fill_color:
        shape.fill.solid()
        shape.fill.fore_color.rgb = fill_color
    else:
        shape.fill.background()
    shape.line.fill.background()
    tf = shape.text_frame
    tf.word_wrap = True
    p = tf.paragraphs[0]
    p.text = text
    p.font.size = Pt(font_size)
    p.font.bold = bold
    p.font.color.rgb = color
    p.alignment = align
    return shape

# ================= SLIDE 1: TITLE =================
slide_layout = prs.slide_layouts[6]  # blank
slide1 = prs.slides.add_slide(slide_layout)
add_background(slide1)

# Accent bar
bar = slide1.shapes.add_shape(MSO_SHAPE.RECTANGLE, Inches(0), Inches(2.8), Inches(13.333), Inches(0.05))
bar.fill.solid()
bar.fill.fore_color.rgb = ACCENT_TEAL
bar.line.fill.background()

add_textbox(slide1, Inches(0.8), Inches(1.8), Inches(11.7), Inches(1.2),
            "TIOBE Index March 2026: How 20+ Search Engines Rank the World's Programming Languages",
            font_size=36, bold=True, color=TEXT_WHITE, align=PP_ALIGN.CENTER)

add_textbox(slide1, Inches(1.0), Inches(3.2), Inches(11.3), Inches(1.0),
            "A data-forward analysis of programming language popularity trends for software engineering leads and technology strategists",
            font_size=20, bold=False, color=TEXT_GRAY, align=PP_ALIGN.CENTER)

add_textbox(slide1, Inches(1.0), Inches(4.5), Inches(11.3), Inches(1.5),
            "Methodology: Ratings are calculated from search-engine hit counts across Google, Amazon, Wikipedia, Bing, and more than 20 other sites.\n"
            "The index reflects how much a language is discussed and sought after on the public internet — not lines of code written.",
            font_size=16, bold=False, color=TEXT_GRAY, align=PP_ALIGN.CENTER)

add_textbox(slide1, Inches(1.0), Inches(6.5), Inches(11.3), Inches(0.5),
            "Source: TIOBE Programming Community Index | Captured: April 10, 2026 | Author: Paul Jansen, CEO, TIOBE Software",
            font_size=12, bold=False, color=TEXT_GRAY, align=PP_ALIGN.CENTER)

# ================= SLIDE 2: TOP 20 RANKINGS =================
slide2 = prs.slides.add_slide(slide_layout)
add_background(slide2)

add_textbox(slide2, Inches(0.5), Inches(0.3), Inches(12.3), Inches(0.7),
            "Python Holds #1 at 21.25% but C Surges to #2 with the Largest Gain",
            font_size=28, bold=True, color=TEXT_WHITE)

add_textbox(slide2, Inches(0.5), Inches(0.9), Inches(12.3), Inches(0.4),
            "Top 20 Programming Languages — March 2026 vs. March 2025",
            font_size=16, bold=False, color=TEXT_GRAY)

# Table data
headers = ["Rank 2026", "Rank 2025", "Language", "Rating", "YoY Change"]
data = [
    ["1", "1", "Python", "21.25%", "-2.59%"],
    ["2", "4", "C", "11.55%", "+2.02%"],
    ["3", "2", "C++", "8.18%", "-2.90%"],
    ["4", "3", "Java", "7.99%", "-2.37%"],
    ["5", "5", "C#", "6.36%", "+1.49%"],
    ["6", "6", "JavaScript", "3.45%", "-0.01%"],
    ["7", "9", "Visual Basic", "2.50%", "-0.02%"],
    ["8", "8", "SQL", "2.00%", "-0.57%"],
    ["9", "16", "R", "1.88%", "+0.94%"],
    ["10", "10", "Delphi/Object Pascal", "1.80%", "-0.36%"],
    ["11", "24", "Perl", "1.75%", "+1.05%"],
    ["12", "12", "Scratch", "1.63%", "-0.03%"],
    ["13", "11", "Fortran", "1.45%", "-0.25%"],
    ["14", "14", "Rust", "1.31%", "+0.09%"],
    ["15", "15", "MATLAB", "1.29%", "+0.31%"],
    ["16", "7", "Go", "1.29%", "-1.49%"],
    ["17", "17", "Assembly language", "1.29%", "+0.42%"],
    ["18", "13", "PHP", "1.23%", "-0.25%"],
    ["19", "18", "Ada", "1.10%", "+0.25%"],
    ["20", "26", "Swift", "1.04%", "+0.44%"],
]

rows = len(data) + 1
cols = len(headers)
table = slide2.shapes.add_table(rows, cols, Inches(0.5), Inches(1.35), Inches(12.3), Inches(5.8)).table

# Set column widths
col_widths = [Inches(1.3), Inches(1.3), Inches(3.2), Inches(1.4), Inches(1.4)]
for i, w in enumerate(col_widths):
    table.columns[i].width = w

# Style header
for i, h in enumerate(headers):
    cell = table.cell(0, i)
    cell.text = h
    cell.fill.solid()
    cell.fill.fore_color.rgb = TABLE_HEADER
    p = cell.text_frame.paragraphs[0]
    p.font.size = Pt(12)
    p.font.bold = True
    p.font.color.rgb = TEXT_WHITE
    p.alignment = PP_ALIGN.CENTER

# Style rows
for r_idx, row in enumerate(data):
    row_color = TABLE_ROW1 if r_idx % 2 == 0 else TABLE_ROW2
    for c_idx, val in enumerate(row):
        cell = table.cell(r_idx + 1, c_idx)
        cell.text = val
        cell.fill.solid()
        cell.fill.fore_color.rgb = row_color
        p = cell.text_frame.paragraphs[0]
        p.font.size = Pt(11)
        p.font.color.rgb = TEXT_WHITE
        p.alignment = PP_ALIGN.CENTER
        # Color YoY changes
        if c_idx == 4:
            if val.startswith("+"):
                p.font.color.rgb = POSITIVE
            elif val.startswith("-") and val != "-":
                p.font.color.rgb = NEGATIVE

add_textbox(slide2, Inches(0.5), Inches(6.35), Inches(12.3), Inches(0.4),
            "The top 4 languages (Python, C, C++, Java) collectively account for 48.97% of the total index.",
            font_size=13, bold=True, color=ACCENT_TEAL)

# ================= SLIDE 3: BIGGEST MOVERS =================
slide3 = prs.slides.add_slide(slide_layout)
add_background(slide3)

add_textbox(slide3, Inches(0.5), Inches(0.3), Inches(12.3), Inches(0.7),
            "Perl Jumps 13 Spots, R Climbs 7, and Go Drops 9 — The Biggest Rank Shifts of 2026",
            font_size=28, bold=True, color=TEXT_WHITE)

# Gainers section
add_textbox(slide3, Inches(0.8), Inches(1.2), Inches(5.5), Inches(0.5),
            "▲ BIGGEST GAINERS", font_size=20, bold=True, color=POSITIVE)

gainers = [
    ("Perl", "24th → 11th", "+1.05%", "+13 spots"),
    ("R", "16th → 9th", "+0.94%", "+7 spots"),
    ("Swift", "26th → 20th", "+0.44%", "+6 spots"),
    ("C", "4th → 2nd", "+2.02%", "+2 spots"),
]

for idx, (lang, rank, change, spots) in enumerate(gainers):
    y = Inches(1.85 + idx * 1.1)
    # Card background
    card = slide3.shapes.add_shape(MSO_SHAPE.ROUNDED_RECTANGLE, Inches(0.8), y, Inches(5.5), Inches(0.9))
    card.fill.solid()
    card.fill.fore_color.rgb = RgbColor(0x1E, 0x33, 0x28)
    card.line.color.rgb = POSITIVE
    card.line.width = Pt(1.5)
    
    add_textbox(slide3, Inches(1.0), y + Inches(0.08), Inches(2.5), Inches(0.4), lang, font_size=18, bold=True, color=POSITIVE)
    add_textbox(slide3, Inches(1.0), y + Inches(0.42), Inches(2.5), Inches(0.3), rank, font_size=14, bold=False, color=TEXT_GRAY)
    add_textbox(slide3, Inches(3.5), y + Inches(0.08), Inches(1.3), Inches(0.4), change, font_size=18, bold=True, color=POSITIVE, align=PP_ALIGN.RIGHT)
    add_textbox(slide3, Inches(3.5), y + Inches(0.42), Inches(1.3), Inches(0.3), spots, font_size=14, bold=False, color=TEXT_GRAY, align=PP_ALIGN.RIGHT)
    add_textbox(slide3, Inches(4.9), y + Inches(0.08), Inches(1.2), Inches(0.7), "▲", font_size=36, bold=True, color=POSITIVE, align=PP_ALIGN.CENTER)

# Losers section
add_textbox(slide3, Inches(7.0), Inches(1.2), Inches(5.5), Inches(0.5),
            "▼ BIGGEST LOSERS", font_size=20, bold=True, color=NEGATIVE)

losers = [
    ("Go", "7th → 16th", "-1.49%", "-9 spots"),
    ("C++", "2nd → 3rd", "-2.90%", "-1 spot"),
    ("Java", "3rd → 4th", "-2.37%", "-1 spot"),
    ("Python", "1st → 1st", "-2.59%", "0 spots"),
]

for idx, (lang, rank, change, spots) in enumerate(losers):
    y = Inches(1.85 + idx * 1.1)
    card = slide3.shapes.add_shape(MSO_SHAPE.ROUNDED_RECTANGLE, Inches(7.0), y, Inches(5.5), Inches(0.9))
    card.fill.solid()
    card.fill.fore_color.rgb = RgbColor(0x33, 0x1E, 0x1E)
    card.line.color.rgb = NEGATIVE
    card.line.width = Pt(1.5)
    
    add_textbox(slide3, Inches(7.2), y + Inches(0.08), Inches(2.5), Inches(0.4), lang, font_size=18, bold=True, color=NEGATIVE)
    add_textbox(slide3, Inches(7.2), y + Inches(0.42), Inches(2.5), Inches(0.3), rank, font_size=14, bold=False, color=TEXT_GRAY)
    add_textbox(slide3, Inches(9.7), y + Inches(0.08), Inches(1.3), Inches(0.4), change, font_size=18, bold=True, color=NEGATIVE, align=PP_ALIGN.RIGHT)
    add_textbox(slide3, Inches(9.7), y + Inches(0.42), Inches(1.3), Inches(0.3), spots, font_size=14, bold=False, color=TEXT_GRAY, align=PP_ALIGN.RIGHT)
    add_textbox(slide3, Inches(11.1), y + Inches(0.08), Inches(1.2), Inches(0.7), "▼", font_size=36, bold=True, color=NEGATIVE, align=PP_ALIGN.CENTER)

# ================= SLIDE 4: HISTORICAL =================
slide4 = prs.slides.add_slide(slide_layout)
add_background(slide4)

add_textbox(slide4, Inches(0.5), Inches(0.3), Inches(12.3), Inches(0.7),
            "From Lisp at #2 in 1986 to Python at #1 in 2026: How Language Rankings Shifted Over Time",
            font_size=26, bold=True, color=TEXT_WHITE)

# Long-term table
hist_headers = ["Language", "2026", "2021", "2016", "2011", "2006", "2001", "1996", "1991", "1986"]
hist_data = [
    ["Python", "1", "3", "5", "7", "8", "26", "17", "—", "—"],
    ["C", "2", "1", "2", "2", "2", "1", "1", "1", "1"],
    ["C++", "3", "4", "3", "3", "3", "2", "2", "2", "9"],
    ["Java", "4", "2", "1", "1", "1", "3", "31", "—", "—"],
    ["C#", "5", "5", "4", "5", "7", "11", "—", "—", "—"],
    ["JavaScript", "6", "7", "8", "10", "10", "8", "33", "—", "—"],
    ["Go", "10", "11", "60", "16", "—", "—", "—", "—", "—"],
    ["Ada", "14", "36", "25", "22", "16", "18", "6", "10", "3"],
    ["Lisp", "26", "34", "26", "13", "14", "19", "8", "4", "2"],
]

rows = len(hist_data) + 1
cols = len(hist_headers)
table2 = slide4.shapes.add_table(rows, cols, Inches(0.5), Inches(1.2), Inches(12.3), Inches(3.0)).table

for i in range(cols):
    table2.columns[i].width = Inches(1.25)

for i, h in enumerate(hist_headers):
    cell = table2.cell(0, i)
    cell.text = h
    cell.fill.solid()
    cell.fill.fore_color.rgb = TABLE_HEADER
    p = cell.text_frame.paragraphs[0]
    p.font.size = Pt(12)
    p.font.bold = True
    p.font.color.rgb = TEXT_WHITE
    p.alignment = PP_ALIGN.CENTER

for r_idx, row in enumerate(hist_data):
    row_color = TABLE_ROW1 if r_idx % 2 == 0 else TABLE_ROW2
    for c_idx, val in enumerate(row):
        cell = table2.cell(r_idx + 1, c_idx)
        cell.text = val
        cell.fill.solid()
        cell.fill.fore_color.rgb = row_color
        p = cell.text_frame.paragraphs[0]
        p.font.size = Pt(11)
        p.font.color.rgb = TEXT_WHITE
        p.alignment = PP_ALIGN.CENTER
        if c_idx == 0:
            p.font.bold = True
            p.alignment = PP_ALIGN.LEFT

# Key insights bullets
add_textbox(slide4, Inches(0.5), Inches(4.4), Inches(12.3), Inches(0.4),
            "Key Historical Patterns (2002–2026)", font_size=18, bold=True, color=ACCENT_GOLD)

insights = [
    "• Python's meteoric rise: From ~8th in 2006 to #1 after 2018, peaking above 25% before settling at 21.25%",
    "• C's resilience: Held a top-2 position for most of the 24-year span, with surges around 2015 and 2025–2026",
    "• Java's long decline: Dominated from 2005–2018 at 25%+, now fallen under 8%",
    "• JavaScript's plateau: Despite web dominance, never exceeded ~5% on TIOBE; currently 3.45%",
    "• C is the only language to remain in the top 2 across all nine measurement points from 1986 to 2026",
]

for idx, insight in enumerate(insights):
    y = Inches(4.9 + idx * 0.45)
    add_textbox(slide4, Inches(0.7), y, Inches(12.0), Inches(0.4), insight, font_size=14, bold=False, color=TEXT_GRAY)

# ================= SLIDE 5: HALL OF FAME =================
slide5 = prs.slides.add_slide(slide_layout)
add_background(slide5)

add_textbox(slide5, Inches(0.5), Inches(0.3), Inches(12.3), Inches(0.7),
            "Python Wins Language of the Year 6 Times — More Than Any Other Language",
            font_size=28, bold=True, color=TEXT_WHITE)

# Winners table
hof_headers = ["Year", "Winner"]
hof_data = [
    ["2025", "C#"],
    ["2024", "Python"],
    ["2023", "C#"],
    ["2022", "C++"],
    ["2021", "Python"],
    ["2020", "Python"],
    ["2019", "C"],
    ["2018", "Python"],
    ["2016", "Go"],
]

rows = len(hof_data) + 1
cols = len(hof_headers)
table3 = slide5.shapes.add_table(rows, cols, Inches(1.0), Inches(1.4), Inches(3.5), Inches(4.0)).table

table3.columns[0].width = Inches(1.2)
table3.columns[1].width = Inches(2.3)

for i, h in enumerate(hof_headers):
    cell = table3.cell(0, i)
    cell.text = h
    cell.fill.solid()
    cell.fill.fore_color.rgb = TABLE_HEADER
    p = cell.text_frame.paragraphs[0]
    p.font.size = Pt(14)
    p.font.bold = True
    p.font.color.rgb = TEXT_WHITE
    p.alignment = PP_ALIGN.CENTER

for r_idx, row in enumerate(hof_data):
    row_color = TABLE_ROW1 if r_idx % 2 == 0 else TABLE_ROW2
    for c_idx, val in enumerate(row):
        cell = table3.cell(r_idx + 1, c_idx)
        cell.text = val
        cell.fill.solid()
        cell.fill.fore_color.rgb = row_color
        p = cell.text_frame.paragraphs[0]
        p.font.size = Pt(13)
        p.font.color.rgb = TEXT_WHITE
        p.alignment = PP_ALIGN.CENTER
        if c_idx == 1 and val == "Python":
            p.font.color.rgb = ACCENT_GOLD
        elif c_idx == 1 and val == "C#":
            p.font.color.rgb = ACCENT_TEAL

# Insights on right side
add_textbox(slide5, Inches(5.5), Inches(1.4), Inches(7.0), Inches(0.5),
            "Awarded to the language with the largest gain in ratings during a calendar year",
            font_size=16, bold=False, color=TEXT_GRAY)

insights5 = [
    ("Python: 6 wins total", "2007, 2010, 2018, 2020, 2021, 2024 — more than any other language in TIOBE history"),
    ("C#: Recent momentum", "Won in both 2023 and 2025, reflecting continued growth driven by the .NET ecosystem"),
    ("Go: From winner to decline", "2016 Language of the Year winner, now fell from 7th to 16th — the sharpest drop in the top 20"),
    ("Note on 2017", "The 2017 winner is not available in the source data"),
]

for idx, (title, desc) in enumerate(insights5):
    y = Inches(2.1 + idx * 1.1)
    add_textbox(slide5, Inches(5.5), y, Inches(7.0), Inches(0.35), title, font_size=17, bold=True, color=TEXT_WHITE)
    add_textbox(slide5, Inches(5.5), y + Inches(0.35), Inches(7.0), Inches(0.5), desc, font_size=14, bold=False, color=TEXT_GRAY)

# ================= SLIDE 6: TAKEAWAYS =================
slide6 = prs.slides.add_slide(slide_layout)
add_background(slide6)

add_textbox(slide6, Inches(0.5), Inches(0.3), Inches(12.3), Inches(0.7),
            "The Top 4 Languages Hold 49% of the Index: What This Means for Your Tech Stack",
            font_size=26, bold=True, color=TEXT_WHITE)

# 5 key takeaway cards
takeaways = [
    ("1. Python: Dominant but declining", 
     "At 21.25%, Python leads by 2× over C, but its -2.59% YoY drop is the largest among the top 5. "
     "Plan for talent retention and watch for ecosystem fragmentation.",
     ACCENT_GOLD),
    ("2. C's resurgence signals systems investment",
     "C gained +2.02% and climbed from 4th to 2nd. For low-level and embedded projects, C expertise is becoming more valuable.",
     ACCENT_TEAL),
    ("3. Legacy languages are reviving",
     "Perl (+13 spots), R (+7 spots), and Fortran (top 15) show entrenched communities in data science and infrastructure.",
     POSITIVE),
    ("4. Go's sharp fall demands caution",
     "Go dropped from 7th to 16th (-1.49%) — the largest absolute drop. Rust (+0.09%) may be displacing it in systems programming.",
     NEGATIVE),
    ("5. Concentration risk in the top 4",
     "Python + C + C++ + Java = 48.97% of the index. Diversifying language investments reduces dependency on a handful of ecosystems.",
     TEXT_WHITE),
]

for idx, (title, desc, color) in enumerate(takeaways):
    y = Inches(1.15 + idx * 1.15)
    # Left accent bar
    bar = slide6.shapes.add_shape(MSO_SHAPE.RECTANGLE, Inches(0.5), y, Inches(0.08), Inches(0.9))
    bar.fill.solid()
    bar.fill.fore_color.rgb = color
    bar.line.fill.background()
    
    add_textbox(slide6, Inches(0.75), y, Inches(11.8), Inches(0.35), title, font_size=17, bold=True, color=color)
    add_textbox(slide6, Inches(0.75), y + Inches(0.35), Inches(11.8), Inches(0.5), desc, font_size=14, bold=False, color=TEXT_GRAY)

add_textbox(slide6, Inches(0.5), Inches(6.8), Inches(12.3), Inches(0.4),
            "Source: TIOBE Programming Community Index — March 2026 | Methodology: Search-engine hit counts across 25+ sites",
            font_size=12, bold=False, color=TEXT_GRAY, align=PP_ALIGN.CENTER)

# Save
os.makedirs("/app/output", exist_ok=True)
prs.save("/app/output/final_deck.pptx")
print("Saved /app/output/final_deck.pptx")
